questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To challenge yourself, and get a place where there was another climate and what im use to in Denmark, and try to live in another city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very hard. I don't think there was a clear communication in the process in workflow of get the exchange paper and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very expensive. I don't think there was no help to get anything cheap. I got some of the cheapest option that the university recommended and it cost 900 euro.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I did not live close to the campus but know that the things recommended by the university is not a student friendly option.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very complicated. No help and very much on your own. My exchange almost got canceled because they "forgot" that i already had send anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you never know if you did anything right or wrong. They almost never answer on anything and you only 1 week before you started get confirmation on your classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i don't think there was help available

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i was very lucky but so stressful registering because you got the confirmation 1 week before you started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do not expect to get your courses. I was lucky but you can't not expect to get your courses in english.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: so bad organized. You could easily do the courses confirmation earlier

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i did both BA and MA and i think in someway the level was low in the class but very high in the exam

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: so bad. Remind me of the way we do it in primary school in Denmark. In Denmark, you have the feeling that teaching at the university is aimed at adults, but in Spain, the teaching felt more like it was directed at children

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

Regnskab analyse

questions.answer: I think Macro III was a good course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was almost nothing. I don't think there was anything. I tried to find som football but there was no option and when i ask there was no help to get.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was something. but did not search for it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: played a lot of sport and enjoy the climate

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: enjoy the climate and the city. The city is so lovely and has some many good restaurants.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was okay but hard with the language because they did not want to speak English

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: play some sports in the local community. For me it was a easy way to do something with other

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the language was a big problem because they did not want to speak english

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the sport and the climate. But also love to eat the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: the weather the football and the food

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: you have to ensure people that they do the right thing in the registration. Very frustrated to not be sure if you did the right things.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: the experiences to try be alone and live in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: to be by my self and try live i another country

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
